title: The 180-minute tutorial
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 3–5 min. Exact notebook modules split 0–20 and 20–45, then 45–65 and 65–85. Total exercise time 51 minutes. There is no additional break inside this 180-minute schedule.

title: Scientific hypotheses
body: Scored feedback improves candidate quality
A separate critic adds value beyond scored feedback
Engineering verification rejects unsafe proposals
Each hypothesis needs its own comparison
foot: A useful workflow can coexist with a stronger conventional optimizer
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 5–9 min. Ask participants which hypothesis can be tested without any LLM. Gate ablation holds the proposed actions fixed.

title: One synthetic Greensboro feeder
foot: The case does not represent a utility operating network
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 9–13 min. Open notebook Figure 1 map. Cite SMART-DS. Distinguish source impedances from constructed operating conditions. Map position does not establish real switching capability.
table: Storage idle, automatic inverter control off
Two synthetic bypasses and critical priorities

title: Provenance and assumptions
body: Original electrical files retain their source hashes
The working copy updates deprecated DSS syntax
Every tenth sorted load receives critical priority
Bypass lines are explicit teaching assumptions
foot: Exercise 1: source fact, assumption or model output? 4 minutes
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 13–20 min. Show source_manifest.json. Exercise 1 from notebook. Source voltage 1.03 pu. Synthetic ties use same source and downstream endpoint, not independent neighboring substations. Instructor answer: coordinates and ratings come from a synthetic model, while priority and bypass designs are invented overlays.

title: Bounded roles in the framework
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 20–25 min. Multiple bounded roles share one installed model. Awareness, simulation and verification are deterministic tools. The system is sequential, not parallel independent model training.

title: The decision state machine
body: Observe and propose a catalog action
Precheck policy and evidence
Simulate a reset feeder and verify constraints
Record every outcome, refine and rank
foot: No feasible candidate produces an explicit no-recommendation outcome
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 25–29 min. Walk through one iteration. There is no unverified fallback. Repeated candidates consume their budget slot. The proposal role cannot edit the simulator or acceptance code.

title: Constrained decision support
body: Choose a ∈ A(x) to maximize J(x, a, f(x,a))
Require every encoded constraint gⱼ(x, a, f(x,a)) ≤ 0
The simulator f produces numerical evidence
The verifier evaluates the acceptance contract
foot: LLM reasoning proposes a candidate; measured results determine its status
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 29–32 min. Define state x, catalog A, simulator f and objective J. Distinguish feasibility from optimality. An optimal point in a restricted catalog is not the global optimum of the physical control problem.

title: What the checker certifies
foot: A passing snapshot has the limits of its model
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 32–37 min. Reachability is bus-level. MV radiality excludes LV secondary meshes. Voltages use a 1e-6 pu tolerance and loading uses 1e-4 percentage-point tolerance. Evidence flags are fixtures with nominal defaults, not actual authentication.

title: Exercise 2: the trust boundary
body: A rationale asks to ignore a line overload
Locate the function that still rejects the action
Identify a missing engineering constraint
Explain the consequence of that missing check
foot: 5-minute exercise, followed by a 3-minute debrief
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 37–45 min. Inspect evaluate and verify_physics in the notebook. Answer: rationale is never executed, metrics determine rejection. A missing transformer or protection constraint can allow a recommendation inadequate for real operations.

title: Llama through the local Ollama server
body: Installed model: llama3.1:8b
Structured JSON from the /api/chat endpoint
Temperature 0.2, explicit seeds, 8,192-token context
The transcript records prompts, responses and costs
foot: 123 actual model calls in the recorded benchmark
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 45–49 min. Sources: https://docs.ollama.com/api/chat and https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/structured-outputs . Exact model digest in metadata.json. One server supports role-specific prompts. Seeds do not guarantee identical results across hardware or runtime versions.

title: The action contract
body: action_id identifies one immutable catalog entry
rationale explains the model’s proposed choice
Unknown IDs fail before an electrical solve
Valid JSON can still describe an unsafe action
foot: The model has no raw-command execution tool
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 49–51 min. Show an actual call record from llama_calls.json. Explain structured output versus physical validity. An unknown ID consumes a slot and returns a precheck failure.

title: Live demonstration: constrained restoration
body: Four Llama proposals on the difficult R2 case
Three additional constraint-critic calls
Independent simulation and verification per candidate
Best verified action or explicit failure
foot: The notebook runs this seven-call demonstration by default
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 51–59 min. Run notebook module 3. Use seed303 by default. Inspect planner text, measured overload and critic feedback. Explain why a critic’s correct prose may still fail to yield a better next action. Saved demo calls are separate from benchmark records.

title: Exercise 3: evidence versus rationale
body: Predict the next action after one rejected proposal
Compare the critic’s explanation with the metrics
Change the seed and retain the complete trace
Record final service and elapsed time
foot: 6 minutes. Failed runs remain part of the evidence
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 59–65 min. A claim of full restoration must match total served_kw/nominal_kw. Critical service alone is not sufficient. Ask each pair to identify one useful or incorrect model statement.

title: Score-conditioned search
body: History stores actions, objectives and failure reasons
The optimizer uses measured outcomes to refine proposals
The critic supplies a separate interpretation of failures
Deterministic ranking chooses among passing actions
foot: OPRO and ReAct motivate the workflow; they do not establish grid safety
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 65–69 min. Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.03409 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629 . Define H_k. The no-critic ablation tests scored history without extra critique. No weight updates occur during the tutorial.

title: Baselines and ablations
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 69–73 min. The reference enumerates eight voltage and ten restoration entries. It is not an AC OPF optimum. Every method uses the same gate. Baseline rules are disclosed, informed heuristics, not secretly generated by Llama.

title: Fairness and measurement
body: Four candidate slots plus one awareness solve per run
Single Llama and no-critic use four model calls
Multi-agent uses seven model calls
Latency and token costs accompany action quality
foot: Equal candidate opportunity is not equal inference compute
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 73–77 min. Invalid proposals consume a slot but skip simulation. Total candidate slots, actual solves and model calls are separate counters. Local timing includes model warm-cache effects. Warmup could affect method ordering.

title: Feasibility and conditional quality
body: Success: at least one verified action in the run
Gap = (catalog reference − best score) / reference
Failed runs have undefined objective gap
Two seeds per scenario support descriptive results
foot: Exercise 4: design an equal-token or equal-time comparison. 5 minutes
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 77–85 min. Explain selection bias if only conditional quality is shown. Include exercise4 final five minutes. Eight runs per method comprise four cases times two seeds, not eight independent networks. A larger study should hold tool access and information constant.

title: Voltage control: physical intuition
body: vⱼ = vᵢ − 2(rP + xQ) + (r² + x²)ℓ
Here v = |V|² and ℓ = |I|²
PV export can reverse branch power flow
The experiments use an unbalanced AC solution
foot: The branch-flow equation explains the trend; OpenDSS evaluates each action
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 85–89 min. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.4865 . Explain assumptions behind the radial equation and why unbalance and losses matter. P positive downstream consumption gives voltage drop, negative export can give rise.

title: V1 and V2: the control problem
body: Maximize measured instantaneous PV generation
V1 uses nominal demand; V2 uses 70% demand
Voltage band and line-current ratings both apply
foot: PV cap is percent of Pmpp, not percent of energy curtailed
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 89–92 min. Reactive power, tap settings and storage are held fixed. This is restricted active-power control, not full Volt/VAR optimization. Energy curtailment requires integration across time.

title: PV production across the action catalog
foot: X-axis: PV cap (% Pmpp). Feasibility must also be checked
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 92–94 min. Open notebook tradeoff scatter plot to see passing and rejected catalog entries. Values are measured kW divided by1000. A high objective at an infeasible point is not a solution.

title: Voltage clearance alone is insufficient
foot: PV 40 clears voltage violations but still overloads lines
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 94–96 min. This is a key safety lesson. Native chart uses actual results, not a schematic. PV30 is the finite-catalog V1 reference.

title: V1: feedback and critic contributions
foot: Seed 101, four candidate slots per method
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 96–99 min. Compare both seeds in the notebook. In this run the critic helps improve the Llama result, while the rule-search baseline also attains the reference. This does not show LLM superiority.

title: Exercise 5: the binding constraint
body: Predict whether PV_40 passes V1
Identify the binding voltage or current constraint
Add PV_35 and recompute the catalog reference
Explain the effect of action-space resolution
foot: 8 minutes, followed by a 3-minute discussion
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 99–110 min. Students can first inspect without editing. The code exercise edits catalog in framework.py, then restarts kernel. Preserve previous evidence as a separate experiment. No claim of global optimality follows from a denser finite grid.

title: Restoration with load priorities
body: Maximize Σᵢ wᵢ Pᵢ zᵢ
Critical-load weight 10, other-load weight 1
Fault isolation, source connectivity and MV radiality
Voltage and current constraints remain active
foot: The objective is weighted nominal kW, not delivered energy
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 110–114 min. Explain binary service z, nominal P, critical weight. The experiment reports total and critical service separately. All grid-following DER in disconnected islands are disabled.

title: Two restoration cases
foot: Synthetic bypasses share the source; they are not independent substations
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 114–117 min. Both bypasses bridge the same source and downstream terminal. Their alternative impedances are teaching assumptions. R2 removes PV and reduces capacity. No utility field topology is inferred.

title: Service restored under the same action rules
foot: R2 full pickup has high service but fails the current limit
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 117–120 min. Never interpret this service chart without feasibility. In R1 short_all passes; in R2 short_all fails. All critical loads survive the synthetic noncritical-shedding actions.

title: R2: the bypass capacity constraint
foot: X-axis: percentage of noncritical load objects disconnected
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 120–122 min. A percentage of load objects does not equal a percentage of demand. Loads have unequal power ratings. Selection is lexicographic, not spatial optimization.

title: R2: feasible restoration and its cost
body: Best catalog action: short_shed_75
Total service: 1.844 MW (38.8%)
Critical service: 100%
Synthetic load disconnects: 1466
foot: Individual load relays are an explicit teaching assumption
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 122–124 min. This high disconnect count is a modeling limitation and a good discussion point. A realistic catalog should use actual sectional switches and include switching burden in the objective.

title: MV radiality and fault quarantine
body: One closed bypass can preserve a radial MV supply
Two parallel bypasses create a cycle
An isolated fault remains unavailable to the planner
A graph check does not certify protective coordination
foot: Exercise 6: replace individual shedding with realistic sections. 8 minutes
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 124–135 min. Explain cycle count on a multigraph, retaining parallel edges. Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.05185 . First three minutes explain, final eight for exercise. Check source connectivity as well as edge count.

title: Cyber-physical threat surfaces
body: Measurements can be stale or inconsistent
Topology and actuator reports can disagree
External notes can contain malicious instructions
A valid action ID can still violate physical limits
foot: The tests distinguish model behavior, physical feasibility and acceptance
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 135–139 min. Source: https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/ai/100/2/e2025/final . Explain prompt injection as untrusted content influencing instructions. These are local fixtures, not live attacks or a production detector.

title: Measurement and provenance fixtures
foot: Timestamp, trust and topology fields are test fixtures, not authenticated telemetry
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 139–143 min. The residual threshold is .01 pu and trusted reference1.03. Source provenance false also rejects. Missing fields use nominal defaults for clean simulation; field software should require explicit validated evidence.

title: Action and actuator fixtures
foot: Readback is a post-action observation; rejection cannot undo an earlier field action
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 143–146 min. The gate ablation applies identical proposals to ungated, catalog-only and full-checker dispositions. No real actuation exists. A field implementation requires rollback or recovery logic for readback mismatch.

title: Three actual prompt-injection trials
foot: Three prompts show observed behavior, not a general robustness rate
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 146–149 min. Inspect the exact notes and model rationales in attacks.json. A safe model action under malicious context is distinct from attack detection. A physical checker may accept a safe action without identifying the injection.

title: Verification ablation
body: Ungated: every proposal survives
Catalog-only: unknown IDs fail
Full checker: policy, evidence and physics also apply
Stealth bias still passes the simple residual test
foot: The proposed action remains identical across the three acceptance columns
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 149–152 min. Show notebook gate_ablation table. Do not label every malicious-input acceptance an unsafe physical action. This experiment isolates the gate contribution, not model superiority.

title: Exercise 7: detection and false alarms
body: Reduce the residual threshold to 0.002 pu
Retest benign noise and stealth bias
Compare model compliance with physical safety
Identify the assumed trusted reference
foot: 8 minutes. The tighter threshold rejects both fixtures
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 152–160 min. The exercise demonstrates false-positive/detection tradeoff. Attack notes can be changed without any field access. A compromised trusted reference requires a different detection design.

title: Feasibility success across the four cases
foot: Eight runs per method: four cases × two seeds
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 160–163 min. Report all outcomes. No-critic failures in R2 are preserved. Different roles sharing one model do not ensure independent reasoning.

title: Extra reasoning has an inference cost
foot: Each search includes one awareness solve; multi-agent also uses three critic calls
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 163–166 min. These are local wall-clock measurements. Rule search is much faster and reaches the catalog reference on these crafted cases. Compare cost as well as feasibility.

title: What the framework demonstrates
body: Structured context makes inputs reproducible
Bounded proposals make actions inspectable
Simulation exposes electrical consequences
Independent verification preserves rejection evidence
foot: Search-quality improvements remain an empirical question
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 166–168 min. The practical result is repeatable, auditable decision support. Automation value could include operator workload reduction, but that requires a user study; it is not measured here.

title: Limits of the scientific evidence
body: One feeder and four constructed snapshots
Two seeds and handcrafted action catalogs
A sequential workflow with shared Llama weights
Simplified load relays and cyber evidence fixtures
foot: The study makes no statistical superiority or deployment-safety claim
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 168–170 min. Add transformer limits, phase-aware connectivity, temporal DER constraints and protection checks before any operational interpretation. Snapshot service is not energy not served.

title: A defensible follow-on experiment
body: Predeclare feeders, cases, seeds and attack families
Compare against AC OPF and discrete restoration optimization
Match information, tool access and computation budgets
Retain failures and measure operator workload separately
foot: Capstone: choose one claimed advantage and design its decisive comparison
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 170–178 min. Two minutes explanation, then first six minutes of capstone. Full capstone has seven minutes including one minute on the references slide. Distinguish generalization from repeated runs on the same case.
